source.title: Function vectors as a model diffing tool: 17 heads repair a bad fine-tune

record.tranche_reason: The post cites the refusal-direction work as inspiration and applies a related direction extraction and intervention to repair a bad-medical-advice fine-tune. Its results concern medical advice safety, not refusal behavior as measured by the claim.
record.gate_note: The direction is extracted from differences between a clean model and a bad-medical-advice fine-tune on medical prompts, not from harmful-minus-harmless instructions. Outcomes are safe/borderline/unsafe medical answers, not refusal rates. The post also reports a direction-probe cosine of approximately 1.0, but this validates the extraction rather than measuring the behavior. The 17-head paste and other repair-method comparisons are not results about the single-direction intervention.
record.test_reason: The post borrows Arditi et al.'s recipe as inspiration: a difference-in-means direction that is removed or added. It applies that recipe to a different construct, bad medical advice. The direction comes from a clean-model versus bad-LoRA-model contrast on medical prompts, not from harmful-minus-harmless instructions. Outcomes are judged safe, borderline or unsafe medical answers, not refusal rates. No result bears on whether refusal is mediated by a single direction, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add the author's explanation, which the author flags as their read and not a result: the LoRA wrote no new compact machinery, so the behavior is spread out. It can be partly removed by restoration but not installed by one direction. The author also concludes that a 17-head paste outperforms the single direction.
record.recipe_differences: The post averages internal states on the same medical prompts for the clean and bad fine-tuned models, subtracts them, then removes or adds the resulting direction. This resembles the cited difference-in-means intervention, but uses a clean-versus-bad-model contrast rather than harmful-versus-harmless instructions. It is an exploratory model-diffing and repair post, not a replication.
record.method_sensitivity: For the Llama head-patching pipeline, the guardrail setting changed the result; the direction-intervention section reports layer and injection-strength conditions, including a layer-15 dose and removal at one layer versus every layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing a clean-versus-bad-model difference-in-means direction partly restores safe medical answers: 1/15 safe becomes 6/15, and 3/36 becomes 10/36. Adding it to the clean model barely beats a matched random direction in judged answers (2 unsafe vs 1), despite a large drop in the multiple-choice logit margin.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A model-diff direction for a narrow misalignment LoRA is partly necessary but not sufficient for the behavior, and logit-margin metrics overstate injection success.

fits_no_version.finding: Direction removal kept ARC-Easy at 100% when done at layer 15 and at 89% when done at every layer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-direction removal of a fine-tune behavior largely preserves capability, with some cost when removed at all layers.

record.problems: Exploratory evidence: one seed, two architectures, narrow LoRA fine-tunes, and medical verdicts from a blind LLM judge on small held-out sets. The direction intervention is on the Qwen medical-advice setting, not refusal. The 15-question table does not identify which removal setting it reports; the 36-question removal comparison lacks a stated baseline and layer setting. ARC-Easy baselines for the direction-removal capability figures are not provided.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for the 17-head paste, few-shot prompting, system prompt, crosscoder, or persona experiments: they do not directly test the single-direction intervention or refusal behavior named in the claim. Direction-probe cosine is mentioned in gate_note because it validates the extracted direction rather than reporting a behavioral outcome.

untested.parts: All parts: no refusal measured, and the direction is not harmful-minus-harmless.
All parts: the weight-baked edit was not built, and refusal was not targeted.
All parts: the multi-unit findings concern medical advice and persona traits, not refusal.
All parts: the Llama transfer concerns head-patching for medical advice, not a refusal direction.
All parts: the LoRA-versus-full-fine-tune speculation is about medical misalignment and is untested.

record.verdict_notes: The post is about function-vector-style model diffing. It cites Arditi et al. only as a methodological template. Its clean-versus-bad medical-advice direction is not a refusal direction, so all rows are correctly linked to none.

versions.untested_parts: No refusal behavior is measured; the direction is not the harmful-minus-harmless instruction difference.
The author says baking the inference-time edit into weights was not built.
No jailbreak suppression or training against ablation is tested.
No refusal mechanism is tested as affine, conic, or multi-directional.
The study does not separately measure harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions.
The direction intervention is not tested across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct transfer.
Only one narrow LoRA fine-tuning recipe is studied; refusal training methods and timing are not compared.
